method: Offline manual review of exact final answers against literal questions; reference facts are secondary, not an automatic correctness score. No reruns. Partial grades are qualitative and do not imply every statement was source-verified.

rows.note: Both correctly distinguish shared lifecycle callers from adapter implementations; A names the concrete adapter hooks more precisely.

Both explain binding and account mismatch. B overgeneralizes that an absent provider account ID leaves the marker empty; bind_account! returns without clearing an existing marker. A explicitly preserves this distinction. Both omit some historical reference details such as UUID column restrictions.
Both identify connection read authorization and enqueueing the export workflow after commit.
Both distinguish firms without uid from contacts/clients with UUID uid; no penalty for omitting an earlier proposed new-column name.
A concentrates on uid/URL naming rather than Instead operation/model conventions; B agrees generically without providing concrete consistent names. A itself acknowledges this mismatch in Q32.

Both answer the literal adapter-entry-point question. The historical reference's exhaustive entry-point list is not required by this short prompt. Wording about a port should not be mistaken for proof of a separate reconcile service.
Both give the worker hierarchy and exhausted-retry failure mapping, and distinguish transfer/webhook workers.
Both identify json-schema/JSON::Validator and named OpenAPI component schemas; B additionally distinguishes the unwired mock router.

B falsely says Crm::Api::Contact.find returns uid; its actual contact_data mapping has no uid. A correctly notes this limitation but pivots to an external HTTP API instead of fully answering the internal CRM API integration question.

Both correctly describe the final unique firm_id index. The initial composite index was removed by the later MakeInsteadConnectionsUniquePerFirm migration, and actor was renamed to creator in a separate later migration. A still calls the polymorphic fields actor_type/actor_id; B correctly says creator. Earlier reviewer criticism based only on the initial migration is superseded.

Both list all nine actual metrics. B's heading says eight while its table contains nine: a minor internal count error. The historical reference also omits entity_matches_total and must not be used to reject the correct nine-item list.
Both address the requested 50 RPM per firm additional rule. B additionally preserves firm-first/app-wide-second ordering. This is a design response, not evidence that code was edited.

A identifies the dedicated zeitwerk.rb overrides, the feature configuration, and the direct send serializer, but omits the two latest-send wrapper serializers. B provides those wrappers but only names general ActiveSupport inflections.rb, omitting the dedicated Zeitwerk initializer. General inflections can affect Rails naming; this is an incomplete repository-specific autoload answer, not proof that inflections.rb has no effect. This explicit Q39 autoload question differs from narrow Q24.
